chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say:
“Whoever intentionally kills himself will be in the Fire of Hell

He was asked: “What if he had made a will and then deliberately killed himself immediately after—will his will be carried out?” He said: “If he made a will before causing any harmful occurrence in himself, whether by a wound or an act, his will is upheld concerning one-third of his estate. But if he made a will after he had already caused in himself a wound or an act by which he may die, his will is not upheld.”

key_terms.ثُلُثِهِ: one-third of his estate, the limit within which the bequest is executed
key_terms.نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ: the Fire of Hell, mentioned as the punishment for intentional self-killing

ai.seo_question: Is the will of a person who intentionally takes his own life valid in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that intentionally taking one’s own life leads to punishment in Hell, emphasizing the grave moral and eschatological seriousness of suicide. It also gives a legal ruling on the validity of a bequest: a waṣiyyah made before self-harm is valid within one-third of the estate, while one made after initiating a fatal self-injury is not valid.
